The symptoms point most directly at **C1**. In this Sallen-Key section (unity-gain follower, feedback cap C1 from node a to vout), a larger C1 lowers the natural frequency, which explains the low fc, and raises Q (Q ∝ √(R1·R2·C1/C2)/(R1+R2)), which explains the high peaking. Neither symptom is explained by a single other passive element without a conflicting effect on the other spec. This is a best estimate from hand analysis, not a simulation, and the 17.3 dB peaking is larger than the passive network alone would produce, so op-amp dynamics may contribute.

This lowers the section's natural frequency, pulling fc below the 912 kHz minimum, and raises its Q, causing the excessive 17.3 dB peaking. Restoring C1 to its nominal value should bring both fc and peaking back into spec."}
